newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- unchanged after data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- unchanged after data.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds showed little reaction Tuesday after economic data indicated a stronger-than-expected consumer sector.
Market participants said activity remains stuck in thin summer trading patterns. "It's still pretty well bid, but thinly offered," one trader said.
The Commerce Department said June retail sales rose 0.5 percent, compared to a downwardly-revised 0.3 percent drop in May.
Economists had expected last month's figure to show a 0.2 percent rise, and U.S. Treasury securities initially dropped after the data.

Fixed income markets recovered, however, as analysts said the data, though an indication of strong consumer demand, would not be enough to convince the Federal Reserve to raise short-term interest rates.
Other data released Tuesday included U.S. chain store sales, which rose 0.9 percent in the week ended July 12, according to BTM/Schroders.
On Wednesday, the market was anticipating the Consumer Price Index for June at 0830 EDT. Economists surveyed by Reuters expected a rise of 0.2 percent both overall and at the core.

The Standard and Poor's Corp Blue List, an indicator of the municipal market's secondary supply, moved slightly higher to $955 million. But it was still low enough to indicate that dealers have been successful in selling off inventories from recent deals.
In futures, September municipal bonds lost 2/32 to 119-10/32, while September Treasury bonds dropped 5/32 to 113-25/32. The MOB spread widened to 177 ticks from 174 at the close Monday.
In the secondary market, Sacramento Municipal Utility District, Calif., MBIA 5-1/8s of 2022 were bid at 5.39 percent, up one basis point from Monday.
Municipal bond sales for Tuesday were expected to total $1.1 billion in 48 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Negotiated offerings total $767 million in 16 sales, with a $350 million Los Angeles Unified School District offering through BancAmerica Securities topping the list.
On the competitive side, 32 sales totaling $363 million are scheduled. A three-part $130.5 million Virginia HDA offering at 1130 EDT is the largest.
